quote: Theorem 1. Let X_i ~ XL(theta_i), i = 1, 2 be two random variables. If theta_1 >= theta_2, then X1 ~lr X2, X1 ~hr X2, X1 ~S X2. (using ~ for the 'smaller than' order symbols printed as \prec_lr, \prec_hr, \prec_S)
family: XLindley distribution XL(theta): f(x; theta) = theta^2 (2 + theta + x) e^{-theta x} / (1 + theta)^2, x > 0, theta > 0 (mixture of Exp(theta) and Lindley(theta))
compared: two XLindley variables with different scale-type parameters theta_1 vs theta_2

conclusion.direction: X1 <=_lr X2 (hence X1 <=_hr X2 and X1 <=_st X2 by Remark 1)
